verses.t: Book of the genesis (biblos geneseōs) of Jesus Anointed, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham begot Isaac, and Isaac begot Jacob, and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers,
and Judah begot Perez and Zerah from Tamar, and Perez begot Hezron, and Hezron begot Aram,
and Aram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, and Nahshon begot Salmon,
and Salmon begot Boaz from Rahab, and Boaz begot Obed from Ruth, and Obed begot Jesse,
and Jesse begot David the king. And David begot Solomon from the [wife] of Uriah,
and Solomon begot Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begot Abijah, and Abijah begot Asaph,
and Asaph begot Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat begot Joram, and Joram begot Uzziah,
and Uzziah begot Jotham, and Jotham begot Ahaz, and Ahaz begot Hezekiah,
and Hezekiah begot Manasseh, and Manasseh begot Amos, and Amos begot Josiah,
and Josiah begot Jeconiah and his brothers, at the deportation of Babylon.
And after the deportation of Babylon, Jeconiah begot Shealtiel, and Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel,
and Zerubbabel begot Abiud, and Abiud begot Eliakim, and Eliakim begot Azor,
and Azor begot Zadok, and Zadok begot Achim, and Achim begot Eliud,
and Eliud begot Eleazar, and Eleazar begot Matthan, and Matthan begot Jacob,
and Jacob begot Joseph the husband of Mary, from whom was begotten Jesus, the one called Anointed.

So all the generations from Abraham until David [are] fourteen generations, and from David until the deportation of Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation of Babylon until the Anointed fourteen generations.
Now of Jesus Anointed the genesis was thus. His mother Mary having been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found having [a child] in [the] womb from [the] Holy Spirit.
And Joseph her husband, being righteous and not willing to expose her, resolved to release her secretly.

But as he was pondering these things — look, an angel of Yahweh appeared to him in a dream, saying: Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take alongside Mary your wife, for the [thing] begotten in her is from [the] Holy Spirit;
and she will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he himself will save his people from their sins.
Now this whole [thing] has happened so that what was spoken by Yahweh through the prophet might be filled full, saying:
"Behold, the virgin will have [a child] in [the] womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel " — which is, being translated, " With us [is] God." (Isa 7:14)
And Joseph, having been raised from sleep, did as the angel of Yahweh ordered him, and took alongside his wife,
and he was not knowing her until she bore a son; and he called his name Jesus.
Now Jesus having been begotten in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king, look, magi from the risings arrived in Jerusalem,
saying, "Where is the one born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in its rising and we came to worship him."
And hearing this, Herod the king was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him,
and gathering all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Anointed is begotten.
And they said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea; for thus it has been written through the prophet:
'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come forth a ruler, who will shepherd my people Israel.'" (Mic 5:2)
Then Herod, secretly having called the magi, determined exactly from them the time of the appearing star,
and sending them to Bethlehem he said, "Going, search out exactly concerning the child; and when y'all find him, report to me, so that I too, coming, may worship him."
And hearing the king, they went; and look, the star which they saw in its rising went before them, until coming it stood over where the child was.
And seeing the star they rejoiced an exceedingly great joy.
And coming into the house they saw the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they worshiped him; and opening their treasures they offered him gifts — gold and frankincense and myrrh.
And being warned in a dream not to circle back to Herod, by another road they withdrew into their own country.

And when they had withdrawn, look, an angel of Yahweh appears in a dream to Joseph, saying, " Rising, take the child and his mother and flee into Egypt, and be there until I tell you; for Herod is about to seek the child, to destroy it."
And rising he took the child and his mother by night and withdrew into Egypt,
and was there until the end of Herod; so that might be filled full what was spoken by Yahweh through the prophet, saying, "Out of Egypt I called my son." (Hos 11:1)

Then Herod, seeing that he had been mocked by the magi, was enraged exceedingly, and sending he did away with all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its districts, from two years old and under, according to the time he had determined exactly from the magi.
Then was filled full what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
"A voice in Ramah was heard, weeping and much mourning; Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more." (Jer 31:15)
And Herod having come to his end, look, an angel of Yahweh appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
saying, " Rising, take the child and his mother and go into the land of Israel; for those seeking the child 's life have died." (Exod 4:19)
And rising he took the child and his mother and entered into the land of Israel.
But hearing that Archelaus reigns over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go off there; and being warned in a dream, he withdrew into the regions of Galilee,
and coming he settled in a city called Nazareth; so that might be filled full what was spoken through the prophets, that he shall be called a Nazarene.
Now in those days there comes-on-the-scene John the Immerser, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea
and saying, " Turn! — for the kingdom of the skies has drawn near."
For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying: "A voice of one crying-out in the wilderness — prepare the way of Yahweh, make straight his paths." (Isa 40:3)
And John himself had his clothing from camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then there went out to him Jerusalem and all Judea and all the surrounding-country of the Jordan,
and they were being immersed in the Jordan river by him, confessing-out their sins.
But seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his immersion, he said to them, "Offspring of vipers! Who warned y'all to flee from the coming wrath?
So then, produce fruit worthy of the turning.
And do not presume to say among yourselves, 'We have Abraham as father.' For I tell y'all that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
And already the axe lies at the root of the trees; so every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
I myself immerse y'all in water unto turning, but the one coming after me is mightier than I — whose sandals I am not fit to carry. He himself will immerse y'all in Holy Spirit and fire,
whose winnowing-fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly-clean his threshing-floor and will gather his wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn-down with unquenchable fire."
Then there comes-on-the-scene Jesus from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be immersed by him.
But John was-trying-to-prevent him, saying, "I have need to be immersed by you, and you come to me?"
But answering, Jesus said to him, " Permit it now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he permits him.
And having been immersed, Jesus immediately went up from the water — and look, the skies were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
And look, a voice out of the skies, saying, "This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I delighted."
Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tested by the slanderer.
And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward he hungered.
And coming, the tester said to him, "If you are Son of God, speak so that these stones may become loaves."
But he, answering, said, "It stands written: 'Not on bread alone shall the human live, but on every word coming out through the mouth of God.'" (Deut 8:3)
Then the slanderer takes him along into the holy city, and he stood him on the pinnacle (little-wing) of the temple,

and says to him, "If you are Son of God, throw yourself down; for it stands written: 'He will command his angels concerning you, and upon their hands they will lift you, lest you strike your foot against a stone.'" (Ps 91:11–12)
Jesus said to him, "Again it stands written: 'You shall not test-out Yahweh your God.'" (Deut 6:16)
Again the slanderer takes him along to a very high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
and said to him, "All these things I will give you, if falling-down you will worship me."
Then Jesus says to him, "Go away, Adversary! For it stands written: 'Yahweh your God you shall worship, and him only shall you serve.'" (Deut 6:13)
Then the slanderer leaves him, and look, angels came and were ministering to him.
Now, having heard that Iōannēs was handed over, he withdrew into the Galilee.
And leaving Nazara behind, having come, he settled in Kapharnaoum- beside-the-sea, in the territories of Zaboulōn and Nephthalim —
so that what was spoken through Ēsaias the prophet might be filled full, saying:
“Land of Zaboulōn and land of Nephthalim, way of the sea, beyond the Jordanēs, Galilee of the nations —
the people, the one sitting in darkness, saw a great light, and to the ones sitting in a region and shadow of death — a light dawned upon them.” (Isa 9:1–2)
From then Jesus began to proclaim and to say: “ Turn, for the kingdom of the skies has drawn near.”
Now, walking beside the sea of the Galilee, he saw two brothers — Simōn the one called Petros, and Andreas his brother — casting a cast-net into the sea; for they were fishers.
And he says to them: “ Come — after me — and I will make y’all fishers of men.”
And they, immediately leaving the nets, followed him.
And going on from there, he saw two other brothers — Iakōbos the son of Zebedaios, and Iōannēs his brother — in the boat with Zebedaios their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
And they, immediately leaving the boat and their father, followed him.
And he went around in the whole of the Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good-news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

And the report of him went out into the whole of Syria; and they brought to him all those having it badly with various diseases and torments — demon-oppressed and moon-struck and paralytic — and he healed them.
And great crowds followed him — from the Galilee and Decapolis and Hierosoluma and Judea and beyond the Jordanēs.
And seeing the crowds he went up onto the mountain; and when he had sat down, his learners came to him.
And opening his mouth he was teaching them, saying:
Blessed are the poor in the spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the skies.
Blessed are the mourning, for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are those hungering and thirsting for righteousness, for they shall be fed full.
Blessed are the loyal-in-love, for they shall be shown loyal-love.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of the skies.
Blessed are y'all whenever they revile y'all and persecute and say every evil thing against y'all, lying, for my sake.
Rejoice and exult, for y'all's wage is much in the skies; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before y'all.
Y'all are the salt of the earth; but if the salt is made foolish, with what will it be salted? It is strong for nothing any longer except, being thrown out, to be trampled underfoot by men.
Y'all are the light of the world. A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden;
nor do they light a lamp and put it under the measuring-bowl, but upon the lampstand, and it shines for all those in the house.
So let y'all's light shine before men, that they may see y'all's good works and glorify y'all's Father who is in the skies.
Do not think that I came to tear down the Law or the Prophets; I came not to tear down but to fulfill.
For amen I say to y'all, until sky and earth pass away, not one iota or one little-stroke shall pass from the Law, until all things come to pass.

Whoever therefore relaxes one of the least of these commandments and so teaches men shall be called least in the kingdom of the skies; but whoever does and teaches them, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of the skies.
For I say to y'all that unless y'all's righteousness abounds beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, y'all shall by no means enter into the kingdom of the skies.
Y'all heard that it was said to the ancients: “You shall not murder; and whoever murders shall be liable to the judgment.”

But I say to y'all that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to the judgment; and whoever says to his brother, “Raca,” shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, “ Fool,” shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
If therefore you are offering your gift upon the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave there your gift before the altar, and go — first be reconciled to your brother, and then come, offer your gift.
Be well-disposed to your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest the adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
Amen I say to you, you shall by no means come out from there until you pay back the last quadrans.
Y'all heard that it was said: “You shall not commit adultery.”
But I say to y'all that everyone who looks at a woman in order to covet her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
And if your right eye trips you up, tear it out and throw it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand trips you up, cut it off and throw it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go away into Gehenna.
And it was said: “Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.”
But I say to y'all that everyone who divorces his wife — except for a matter of sexual immorality — makes her commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Again, y'all heard that it was said to the ancients: “You shall not swear falsely, but shall render to Yahweh your oaths.”
But I say to y'all not to swear at all: neither by sky, for it is God's throne;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor toward Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King;
nor by your head shall you swear, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let y'all's word be “yes, yes,” “no, no”; and what is beyond these is from the evil one.
Y'all heard that it was said: “An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.”
But I say to y'all not to resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also;
and to the one wanting to sue you and take your tunic, let him have also your cloak;
and whoever will compel you to go one mile, go with him two.
To the one asking you, give; and the one wanting to borrow from you, do not turn away.
Y'all heard that it was said: “You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.”
But I say to y'all, love y'all's enemies and pray for those persecuting y'all,
so that y'all may become sons of y'all's Father who is in the skies, for he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good and rains on the just and the unjust.
For if y'all love those loving y'all, what wage have y'all? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if y'all greet only y'all's brothers, what extraordinary thing do y'all do? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
Y'all therefore shall be whole as y'all's Father in the skies is whole.
“But watch out that y’all don’t do y’all’s right-doing in front of people, toward the end of being gazed at by them; otherwise y’all have no wage alongside y’all’s Father, the one in the skies.

“So whenever you do a mercy-deed, don’t blow a trumpet ahead of yourself, the way the stage-actors do in the meeting-houses and in the alleys, so that they may be glorified by people. Amen I say to y’all: they have their wage in full.
“But you, when you are doing a mercy-deed, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your mercy-deed may be in the hidden place; and your Father, the one seeing in the hidden place, will pay you back.”

“And whenever y’all pray, y’all will not be like the stage-actors, because they love to stand and pray in the meeting-houses and on the corners of the wide streets, so that they may appear to people. Amen I say to y’all: they have their wage in full.

“But you, whenever you pray, go into your storeroom and, having shut your door, pray to your Father, the one in the hidden place; and your Father, the one seeing in the hidden place, will pay you back.
“And when praying, don’t babble-on the way the nations do, for they suppose that in their many-wordiness they will be listened to.
So don’t be made like them, for y’all’s Father has known what things y’all have need of before y’all ask him.
“So pray like this, y’all:
“For if y’all release for people their false steps, y’all’s Father in the skies will also release for y’all;
but if y’all do not release for people, neither will y’all’s Father release y’all’s false steps.”

“And whenever y’all fast, don’t become gloomy-faced like the stage-actors, for they un-appear their faces so that they may appear to people as fasting. Amen I say to y’all: they have their wage in full.
“But you, when fasting, oil your head and wash your face,
so that you may not appear to people as fasting, but to your Father, the one in the hidden place; and your Father, the one seeing in the hidden place, will pay you back.
“Don’t treasure up for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and eating make them vanish, and where thieves dig through and steal;
but treasure up for yourselves treasures in sky, where neither moth nor eating makes them vanish, and where thieves do not dig through nor steal.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
“The lamp of the body is the eye. So if your eye is single, your whole body will be full of light;
but if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If, then, the light in you is darkness — the darkness, how much!”

“No one is able to slave for two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold fast to one and look down on the other. Y’all are not able to slave for God and for Mammon.”

“Because of this I say to y’all: don’t be pulled apart with care for y’all’s life — what y’all will eat — nor for y’all’s body — what y’all will put on. Isn’t the life more than the food, and the body more than the clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and y’all’s Father in the skies feeds them. Aren’t y’all worth more than they?
And which of y’all, by being pulled apart with care, is able to add one forearm’s length to his span?
And about clothing — why are y’all pulled apart with care? Study the wildflowers of the field, how they grow: they do not labor nor spin.
But I say to y’all that not even Solomon in all his glory was wrapped like one of these.
And if God so clothes the grass of the field — here today and tomorrow thrown into an oven — will he not much more clothe y’all, y’all little-faiths?
So don’t be pulled apart with care, saying ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wrap ourselves in?’
For all these things the nations seek after; for y’all’s Father in the skies has known that y’all need all of these.
But seek first the kingdom and his right-doing, and all these things will be added to y’all.
So don’t be pulled apart with care for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be pulled apart with care about itself. Enough for the day is its own trouble.”
Don't y'all judge, so that y'all not be judged.
For with whatever verdict y'all judge, y'all will be judged; and with whatever measure y'all measure out, it will be measured back to y'all.
And why do you stare at the wood-chip in your brother's eye, but the roof-beam in your own eye — you don't even take it in?
Or how will you say to your brother, " Let me throw out the wood-chip from your eye " — and look, the roof-beam is in your own eye!
Mask-wearer! Throw out the roof-beam from your own eye first, and then you'll see clear through to throw out the wood-chip from your brother's eye.
Don't y'all give the holy thing to the dogs, and don't throw y'all's pearls out in front of the pigs — or else they'll stomp them down with their feet, and wheel around and rip y'all open.
Ask — and it will be given to y'all. Seek — and y'all will find. Knock — and it will be opened to y'all.
For everyone asking receives, and the one seeking finds, and to the one knocking it will be opened.
Or what person is there among y'all whose son will ask him for a loaf — he won't hand him a stone, will he?
Or he'll ask for a fish — he won't hand him a snake, will he?
So if y'all, being evil, know how to give good gifts to y'all's children, how much more will y'all's Father — the one in the skies — give good things to those asking him!
So then — everything, however much y'all want people to do to y'all, that's what y'all do to them. For this is the Law and the Prophets.
Come in through the narrow gate. Because wide is the gate and roomy is the road that leads off into ruin — and many are the ones coming in through it.
Because narrow is the gate and squeezed is the road that leads off into life — and few are the ones who find it.
Keep yourselves clear of the sham-prophets, who come at y'all dressed in sheep's wool but underneath are wolves — wolves out to prey.
From their fruits y'all will recognize them. They don't gather grapes off thornbushes, or figs off thistles, do they?
So every good tree makes fine fruit, but the rotten tree makes evil fruit.
A good tree cannot make evil fruits, and a rotten tree cannot make fine fruits.
Every tree not making fine fruit is chopped down and thrown into fire.
So then — from their fruits y'all will recognize them.
Not everyone saying to me "Master! Master!" will come into the kingdom of the skies — but the one doing the will of my Father, the one in the skies.
Many will say to me on that Day: "Master! Master! Didn't we prophesy by your name — and by your name throw out demons — and by your name make many acts of power?"
And then I'll declare to them: "I never knew y'all. Get away from me, y'all workers of lawlessness." (Ps 6:8)
So everyone — whoever hears these words of mine and does them — will be likened to a shrewd man, who built his house on the rock.
And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew and hurled themselves at that house — and it did not fall, for it had been founded on the rock.
And everyone hearing these words of mine and not doing them will be likened to a stupid man, who built his house on the sand.
And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew and slammed into that house — and it fell. And its fall was enormous.
And it happened, when Jesus finished these words, the crowds were knocked clean out of themselves at his teaching.
For he was teaching them as one having authority — and not like their scribes.
And as he was coming down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
And look — a leprous man, coming up, kept bowing low before him, saying, "Master, if you are willing, you have the power to cleanse me."
And stretching out the hand he took hold of him, saying, "I am willing — be cleansed." And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
And Jesus says to him, "See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest and bring the gift Moses ordered — as evidence for them."
And as he was entering Capernaum a centurion came up to him, urging him
and saying, "Master, my boy has been thrown down in the house, paralyzed, dreadfully tormented."
And he says to him, "I myself will come and heal him."
And answering, the centurion said, "Master, I am not big enough for you to come under my roof; but only say it with a word, and my boy will be cured.
For I myself am a man set under authority, with soldiers under me, and I say to this one 'March,' and he marches, and to another 'Come,' and he comes, and to my slave 'Do this,' and he does it."
And hearing this, Jesus marveled and said to those following, "Amen I tell y'all, with no one in Israel have I found such trust.
And I tell y'all that many will arrive from the risings and the settings and will recline at table with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of the skies,
but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the darkness outside; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth."
And Jesus said to the centurion, "Go — as you trusted, let it happen for you." And the boy was cured in that hour.
And coming into Peter's house, Jesus saw his mother-in-law thrown down and burning with fever.
And he took hold of her hand, and the fever released her, and she was raised and began waiting on him.
And when evening came, they brought him many who were demon-possessed; and he threw the spirits out with a word, and healed all who were in a bad way —
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be filled full: "He himself took our weaknesses and carried off our diseases." (Isa 53:4)
And seeing large crowds around him, Jesus gave the order to go off to the other side.
And one scribe, coming up, said to him, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go off to."
And Jesus says to him, "The foxes have burrows and the birds of the sky have roosts, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lean his head."
And another of the learners said to him, "Master, let me first go off and bury my father."
But Jesus says to him, " Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
And as he stepped into the boat, his learners followed him.
And look — a great shaking happened in the sea, so that the boat was being buried under the waves; but he himself was sleeping.
And coming up they roused him, saying, "Master, save — we are being destroyed!"
And he says to them, "Why are y'all cowards, y'all little-faiths?" Then, having been raised, he charged the winds and the sea sharply, and there was a great stillness.
And the people marveled, saying, "What sort of being is this, that even the winds and the sea listen under him?"
And when he came to the other side, into the country of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tombs — so dangerous that no one had the strength to pass by along that road.
And look — they screamed, saying, "What is there between us and you, Son of God? Did you come here to torment us before the appointed time?"
Now far off from them there was a herd of many pigs, grazing.
And the demons kept urging him, saying, "If you throw us out, send us off into the herd of pigs."
And he said to them, "Go." And coming out, they went off into the pigs. And look — the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the waters.
And the herdsmen fled, and going off into the city they reported everything, including the business of the demon-possessed men.
And look — the whole city came out to meet Jesus, and seeing him they urged him to move on away from their borders.
And getting into a boat, he crossed over and came into his own city.
And look — they were carrying to him a paralyzed man, thrown on a mat. And Jesus, seeing their trust, said to the paralyzed man: " Take heart, child — your sins are released."
And look — some of the scribes said among themselves: "This man defames."
And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said: "Why are y'all thinking evil in y'all's hearts?
For which is easier — to say 'Your sins are released,' or to say ' Get up and walk'?
But so that y'all may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to release sins " — then he says to the paralyzed man: " Get up, pick up your mat, and go away to your house."
And getting up, he went away to his house.
And the crowds, seeing it, were afraid, and gave honour to God, who had given such authority to human beings.
And as Jesus was passing on from there, he saw a man sitting at the toll booth, called Matthew, and says to him: " Follow me." And getting up, he followed him.
And it happened, as he reclined at table in the house, look — many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined at table together with Jesus and his learners.
And the Pharisees, seeing it, were saying to his learners: "Why does y'all's teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
But he, hearing it, said: "Those who are strong have no need of a healer, but those who are sick do.
But go and learn what this is: 'I want loyal-love and not sacrifice.' (Hos 6:6) For I didn't come to call the upright, but sinners."
Then John's learners come to him, saying: "Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your learners don't fast?"

And Jesus said to them: "The sons of the wedding-hall can't mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them, can they? But days will come when the bridegroom is torn away from them, and then they will fast."
And no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on a worn-out cloak — for its patch tears away from the cloak, and a worse tear happens.

Nor do people pour new wine into worn-out skins — otherwise, the skins burst, and the wine spills out, and the skins are destroyed. But they pour new wine into fresh skins, and both are kept safe together.
While he was saying these things to them, look — a certain ruler came and knelt low before him, saying: "My daughter has just died — but come, lay your hand on her, and she will live."
And Jesus got up and began following him, and his learners too.
And look — a woman hemorrhaging for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak.
For she was saying to herself: "If I only touch his cloak, I will be saved."
And Jesus, turning and seeing her, said: " Take heart, daughter — your trust has saved you." And the woman was saved from that hour.
And Jesus, coming into the ruler's house, and seeing the flute-players and the crowd in commotion,
was saying: "Y'all clear out — the little girl hasn't died, she's sleeping." And they were laughing at him.
But when the crowd had been thrown out, he went in and took hold of her hand, and the little girl was raised.
And this news went out into that whole land.
And as Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: "Have loyal-love on us, Son of David!"
And when he had come into the house, the blind men came up to him, and Jesus says to them: "Do y'all trust that I'm able to do this?" They say to him: "Yes, Master."
Then he touched their eyes, saying: "According to y'all's trust, let it be to y'all."
And their eyes were opened. And Jesus snorted at them with strong feeling, saying: "See that no one knows."
But going out, they spread the news about him in that whole land.
And as they were going out, look — they brought to him a mute man, possessed by a demon.
And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds were amazed, saying: "Never has it appeared like this in Israel."
But the Pharisees were saying: "By the ruler of the demons he casts out demons."
And Jesus was going around all the towns and the villages, teaching in their gathering-places and proclaiming the good-news of the kingdom and tending every disease and every weakness.
And seeing the crowds, he was wrenched in the gut over them, because they were harassed and flung down like sheep that have no shepherd.
Then he says to his learners: "The harvest indeed is much, but the workers are few.
So beg the Master of the harvest that he may thrust out workers into his harvest."
And summoning his twelve learners, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, so as to throw them out and to tend every disease and every weakness.
And of the twelve emissaries the names are these: first Simon, the one called Rock, and Andrew his brother; and Jacob the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax-collector; Jacob the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot — the very one who handed him over.
These twelve Jesus sent out, ordering them, saying: "Onto a road of the nations do not go off, and into a town of Samaritans do not enter;
go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
And going, proclaim, saying that 'The kingdom of the skies has drawn near.'
Tend the weak, raise the dead, cleanse the leprous, throw out demons. As a gift y'all received; as a gift give.
Do not acquire gold, nor silver, nor copper for y'all's belts;
no travelling-bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff — for the worker is worthy of his food.
And into whatever town or village y'all enter, search out who in it is worthy, and stay there until y'all go out.
And entering into the house, greet it;
and if indeed the house is worthy, let y'all's peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let y'all's peace turn back to y'all.
And whoever does not receive y'all nor hear y'all's words — going out of that house or that town, shake off the dust of y'all's feet.
Amen I say to y'all: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
"Look — I myself am sending y'all out as sheep in the middle of wolves. So become shrewd as the snakes and unalloyed as the doves.
And beware of the people; for they will hand y'all over to councils, and in their gathering-places they will flog y'all;
and before governors and even kings y'all will be led, for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the nations.
And whenever they hand y'all over, do not be pulled apart with care how or what y'all should speak; for it will be given to y'all in that hour what to speak;
for it is not y'all who are the ones speaking, but the Spirit of y'all's Father, the one speaking in y'all.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father a child; and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.
And y'all will be hated by everyone on account of my name; but the one enduring to the end — this one will be saved.
And whenever they pursue y'all in this town, flee to the other; for amen I say to y'all, y'all will not finish the towns of Israel until the Son of Man comes.
A learner is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.
Enough for the learner that he become as his teacher, and the slave as his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzeboul, how much more his household!
So do not fear them; for nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and hidden that will not be known.
What I say to y'all in the dark, speak in the light; and what y'all hear in the ear, proclaim upon the rooftops.
And do not fear those killing the body but unable to kill the life; fear rather the one able to destroy both life and body in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall onto the ground apart from y'all's Father.
And of y'all even the hairs of the head are all numbered.
So do not fear; y'all are worth more than many sparrows.
Everyone, then, who will acknowledge me before the people, I too will acknowledge him before my Father in the skies;
and whoever disowns me before the people, I too will disown him before my Father in the skies.
"Do not suppose that I came to throw peace onto the earth; I did not come to throw peace, but a sword.
For I came to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a bride against her mother-in-law;
and a man's enemies will be the members of his own household." (Mic 7:6)
The one loving father or mother above me is not worthy of me; and the one loving son or daughter above me is not worthy of me;
and whoever does not take up his cross and follow behind me is not worthy of me.
The one finding his life will lose it, and the one losing his life for my sake will find it.
"The one receiving y'all receives me, and the one receiving me receives the one who sent me.
The one receiving a prophet in the name of a prophet will take a prophet's wage; and the one receiving a just person in the name of a just person will take a just person's wage.
And whoever gives one of these small ones only a cup of cold water to drink, in the name of a learner — amen I say to y'all, he will certainly not lose his wage."
And it happened, when Jesus finished laying out orders for his twelve learners, he moved on from there to teach and to proclaim in their towns.
Now John, having heard in the jailhouse of the deeds of the Anointed One, having sent through his learners,
said to him, "Are you the one who is coming, or should we keep expecting a different one?"
And answering, Jesus said to them, "Having gone, report to John what y'all hear and see:
blind people see again and lame people walk around, lepers are made clean and the deaf hear, and dead people are raised, and poor people are told good-news.
And blessed is whoever is not tripped up by me."
Now as these were going away, Jesus began to say to the crowds concerning John, "What did y'all go out into the wilderness to gaze at? A reed shaken by wind?
But what did y'all go out to see? A man dressed in soft things? Look — those who wear soft things are in kings' houses.
But what did y'all go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell y'all, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it stands written: 'Look, I send out my messenger before your face, who will clear your road ahead of you.'"
Amen I tell y'all, among those born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Immerser; but the smaller-one in the kingdom of the skies is greater than he.
And from the days of John the Immerser until now, the kingdom of the skies is under assault, and forceful people seize it.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John;
and if y'all are willing to receive it, this one is Elijah, the one who is about to come.
The one who has ears, let him hear.
"But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call out to the others,
saying: 'We played the flute for y'all, and y'all did not dance; we sang a dirge, and y'all did not beat y'all's chests.'
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look — a gluttonous man and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!' And Wisdom was shown to be in the right by her deeds."
Then he began to reproach the towns in which most of his acts of power had happened, because they did not turn.
"Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Because if the acts of power that happened in y'all had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned long ago, in sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell y'all, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for y'all.
And you, Capernaum — will you be lifted up to the sky? You will go down to Hades. Because if the acts of power that happened in you had happened in Sodom, it would have remained until today.
But I tell y'all that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment, than for you."
At that season, answering, Jesus said, "I openly acknowledge you, Father, Yahweh of the sky and the earth, because you hid these things from wise and perceptive people, and revealed them to infants.
Yes, Father, because thus it was well-pleasing before you.
All things were handed over to me by my Father, and no one fully knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone fully know the Father except the Son and whomever the Son wishes to reveal him to."
Come here to me, all who are laboring and having been burdened, and I will give y'all rest.
Take my yoke upon y'all and learn from me, because I am gentle and lowly in heart, and y'all will find rest for y'all's beings.
For my yoke does you good, and my burden is light."
In that season Jesus went on the Sabbaths through the grainfields. His learners were hungry, and they began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
But the Pharisees, seeing it, said to him, "Look, your learners are doing what is not permitted to do on a Sabbath."
He said to them, "Did y'all not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him —
how he went into the house of God and they ate the loaves of the presentation, which was not permitted for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?
Or did y'all not read in the Law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple treat the Sabbath as common and are guiltless?
I say to y'all: something greater than the temple is here.
And if y'all had known what this is — ' Loyal-love I want, and not sacrifice' (Hos 6:6) — y'all would not have condemned the guiltless.
For master of the Sabbath is the Son of Man."
Moving on from there, he came into their gathering-place.
And look — a person having a withered hand. And they questioned him, saying, "Is it permitted on the Sabbaths to heal?" — so that they might accuse him.
He said to them, "What person will there be among y'all who will have one sheep, and if it falls on the Sabbaths into a pit, will he not take hold of it and raise it?
How much, then, a person differs from a sheep! So it is permitted on the Sabbaths to do well."
Then he says to the person, " Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy as the other.
But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
But Jesus, knowing it, withdrew from there. And many followed him, and he healed them all,
and he charged them sharply that they not make him manifest,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be filled full, saying:
"Look, my servant whom I chose, my beloved, in whom my being delighted. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce judgment to the nations. (Isa 42:1)
He will not quarrel, nor cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the broad streets. (Isa 42:2)
A crushed reed he will not break, and a smouldering wick he will not quench, until he throws out judgment to victory. (Isa 42:3)
And in his name nations will hope." (Isa 42:4)
Then a demonized man, blind and mute, was brought to him; and he healed him, so that the mute man spoke and saw.
And all the crowds were beside themselves and were saying, "This one isn't the Son of David, is he?"
But the Pharisees, hearing it, said, "This one does not throw out the demons except by Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons."
Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is made a wilderness, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
And if the Adversary throws out the Adversary, he was divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?
And if I throw out the demons by Beelzeboul, by whom do y'all's sons throw them out? For this reason they will be y'all's judges.
But if by the Spirit of God I throw out the demons, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon y'all.
Or how can anyone go into the house of the strong man and seize his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he will plunder his house.
The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.
For this reason I say to y'all: every sin and defaming will be released to people, but the defaming of the Spirit will not be released.

And whoever says a word against the Son of Man, it will be released to him; but whoever says a word against the Holy Spirit, it will not be released to him, neither in this age nor in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for by the fruit the tree is known.
Offspring of vipers! How can y'all speak good things, being evil? For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
The good person out of the good treasure throws out good things, and the evil person out of the evil treasure throws out evil things.
I say to y'all that every workless word that people will speak, they will give back an account of it in the day of judgment.
For by your words you will be shown to be in the right, and by your words you will be condemned."
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, "Teacher, we want to see a sign from you."
He answered and said to them, "An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster three days and three nights (Jonah 1:17), so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
Men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation and will judge against it, because they turned at the proclamation of Jonah — and look, something more than Jonah is here.

The queen of the south will be raised in the judgment with this generation and will judge against it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon — and look, something more than Solomon is here.
Whenever the unclean spirit goes out from the person, it goes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it.
Then it says, 'Into my house I will go back, from where I came out.' And coming, it finds it vacant, swept, and put in order.

Then it goes and takes along with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and going in they settle there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will be also for this evil generation."
While he was still speaking to the crowds, look — his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
[Someone said to him, "Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to you."]
He answered and said to the one telling him, "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?"
And stretching out his hand over his learners, he said, "Look — my mother and my brothers.
For whoever does the will of my Father in the skies, that one is my brother and sister and mother."
On that day Jesus, going out of the house, was sitting beside the sea.
And many crowds were gathered to him, so that he stepped into a boat to sit, and the whole crowd was standing on the beach.
And he spoke to them many things in parables, saying: "Look — the sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured them.
Others fell on the rock-like ground, where it did not have much earth, and immediately it sprang up, because of not having depth of earth.
But when the sun had risen it was scorched, and because of not having root it withered.
Others fell on the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.
Others fell on the good earth and kept giving fruit — one a hundred, one sixty, one thirty.
The one having ears — let him hear."
And the learners came near and said to him, "Why do you speak to them in parables?"
He answered and said to them, "Because to y'all it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of the skies, but to those it has not been given.
For whoever has, it will be given to him and he will overflow; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
For this reason I speak to them in parables: because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is being filled up, which says: 'With hearing y'all will hear and by no means understand; and seeing y'all will see and by no means perceive.

For the heart of this people has been made thick, and with their ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they have shut — lest they perceive with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with the heart and turn back — and I will heal them.' (Isa 6:9–10)
But y'all's eyes are blessed, because they see, and y'all's ears, because they hear.
For amen I say to y'all: many prophets and righteous ones longed to perceive what y'all see and did not perceive, and to hear what y'all hear and did not hear.
Y'all, then, hear the parable of the sower.
Anyone hearing the word of the kingdom and not understanding — the evil one comes and snatches what was sown in his heart. This is the one sown beside the road.
And the one sown on the rock-like ground — this is the one hearing the word and immediately receiving it with joy;
but he does not have root in himself; rather, he is for-a-season, and when pressure or persecution comes because of the word, immediately he is tripped up.
And the one sown into the thorns — this is the one hearing the word, and the care that pulls apart, of the age, and the deceit of wealth choke the word, and it becomes fruitless.
And the one sown on the good earth — this is the one hearing the word and understanding, who indeed bears fruit and makes — one a hundred, one sixty, one thirty."
Another parable he set before them, saying: "The kingdom of the skies was likened to a man sowing good seed in his field.
But while the people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed darnel over, in the midst of the wheat, and went away.
And when the blade sprouted and made fruit, then the darnel also showed itself.
And the slaves of the master of the house came near and said to him, 'Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where, then, does it have darnel?'
And he said to them, 'An enemy person did this.' And the slaves say to him, 'Do you want us, then, to go off and collect them?'
But he says, 'No — lest while collecting the darnel y'all uproot the wheat along with them.

Let both grow together until the harvest; and in the season of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Collect first the darnel and bind them into bundles for burning them up, but the wheat gather into my barn.'"
Another parable he set before them, saying: "The kingdom of the skies is like a grain of mustard, which a man took and sowed in his field —
which is smaller than all the seeds, but when it has grown it is greater than the garden-plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches."
Another parable he spoke to them: "The kingdom of the skies is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three seahs of flour, until the whole was leavened."
All these things Jesus spoke in parables to the crowds, and without a parable he was speaking nothing to them —
so that what was spoken through the prophet might be filled full, saying: 'I will open my mouth in parables; I will pour out things hidden since the foundation.' (Ps 78:2)
Then, leaving the crowds, he went into the house. And his learners came near to him, saying, "Make clear to us the parable of the darnel of the field."
He answered and said, "The one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man;
and the field is the world; and the good seed — these are the sons of the kingdom; and the darnel are the sons of the evil one;
and the enemy who sowed them is the slanderer; and the harvest is the completion of an age; and the reapers are angels.
So just as the darnel is collected and burned up with fire, so it will be at the completion of the age.
The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will collect out of his kingdom all the trip-traps and those doing lawlessness,
and they will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth.
Then the righteous will blaze out like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. The one having ears — let him hear.
The kingdom of the skies is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid; and from his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of the skies is like a merchant man seeking fine pearls;
and having found one very precious pearl, he went off and has sold all that he had, and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of the skies is like a dragnet thrown into the sea and gathering from every kind;
which, when it was filled full, they hauled up onto the beach, and sitting down they collected the good into containers, but the rotten they threw outside.
So it will be at the completion of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from the midst of the righteous,
and they will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth.
"Have y'all understood all these things?" They say to him, "Yes."
And he said to them, "For this reason every scribe made a learner for the kingdom of the skies is like a man, a master of the house, who throws out of his treasure-store new things and old."
And it happened, when Jesus completed these parables, he moved on from there.

And having come into his hometown, he was teaching them in their gathering-place, so that they were struck out of themselves and were saying, “From where does this man get this wisdom and the acts of power?
Isn’t this the builder’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And his sisters — aren’t they all here with us? From where, then, does this man get all these things?”
And they kept being tripped up in him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his own house.”
And he did not do many acts of power there, because of their not-trusting.
At that season Herod the quarter-ruler heard the report about Jesus,
and he said to his servants, “This is John the Immerser. He has been raised from the dead, and that is why the acts of power are at work in him.”
For Herod, having seized John, bound him and put him away in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother;
for John had been saying to him, “It is not permitted for you to have her.”
And though he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him as a prophet.
But when Herod’s birthday feast came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the middle and pleased Herod,
so that he declared with an oath to give her whatever she might ask.
And she, coached by her mother, says, “ Give me, here, on a platter, the head of John the Immerser.”
And the king, grieved, because of the oaths and those reclining at table with him, commanded it to be given,
And he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
And his head was brought on a platter and given to the little girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And his learners came and took up the corpse and buried him, and they went and reported to Jesus.
And Jesus, having heard, withdrew from there in a boat to a wilderness place privately; and the crowds, having heard, followed him on foot from the towns.
And coming out, he saw a large crowd, and he was wrenched in the gut over them, and he healed their sick.
When evening came, the learners came to him saying, “The place is wilderness, and the hour has already gone by. Send the crowds away, so that they can go into the villages and buy themselves food.”
But Jesus said to them, “They have no need to go away. Y’all yourselves give them something to eat.”
They say to him, “We have nothing here but five loaves and two fish.”
And he said, “Bring them here to me.”

And commanding the crowds to lean back on the grass, taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up into the sky, he spoke the blessing, and breaking the loaves he gave them to the learners, and the learners to the crowds.
And they all ate and were fed full, and they took up the surplus of the broken pieces: twelve baskets full.
And those eating were men, about five thousand, apart from women and children.
And at once he compelled the learners to get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, until he should send the crowds away.
And having sent the crowds away, he went up into the mountain privately to pray. When evening came, he was there alone.
But the boat was already many stadia away from the land, tormented by the waves, for the wind was against it.
In the fourth watch of the night he came toward them, walking on the sea.
But the learners, seeing him walking on the sea, were thrown into turmoil, saying, “It’s an apparition!” and from fear they cried out.
But at once Jesus spoke to them, saying, “ Take heart: I am. Do not fear.”
Peter answered him and said, “Master, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”
And he said, “Come.” And Peter, going down from the boat, walked on the waters and came toward Jesus.
But seeing the wind, strong, he was afraid, and beginning to be swallowed by the deep, he cried out, saying, “Master, save me!”
And at once Jesus, stretching out his hand, took hold of him and says to him, “ Little-faith, why did you waver?”
And when they had gone up into the boat, the wind wore itself out.
And those in the boat worshiped him, saying, “Truly you are God’s Son.”
And having crossed over, they came onto land at Gennesaret.
And the men of that place, recognizing him, sent into all that surrounding region and brought to him all who were in a bad way,
and they kept urging him that they might only touch the fringe of his cloak; and as many as touched were brought safely through.
